fatigue.detail: Plain rolled bottom flange; welded attachments are checked separately in the detail register.

notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 5 simply supported 18-ft bays, W18X86 girders, one 12.5-ton pendant crane, on new freestanding W14X370 columns with built-up tapered I haunches, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-flange 1.43, saddle-across-fatigue 1.12 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The bracket stays: the W10X49 crane-level strut is moment-connected in plan at every column by 0.5 in plates on its flanges (torsion brace, 2 rows of bolt pairs) and holds the new W14X370 columns against the twist: 0.0035 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 0.091 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.877 in). The strut is sized so the girder's twist movement under the factored traction, 0.091 in, is within 0.125 in (a configurator target, the TR-13 alignment tolerance class, not a code limit). With the strut on the column centerline alone, the girder seated 31.95 in off the column axis, the traction twists the column 0.0244 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 0.626 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.877 in).

selections.designed: Paired flat bars on a bearing-stiffener gusset
selections.reason: A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-flange 1.43, saddle-across-fatigue 1.12 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.82, vertical deflection 0.30, lateral 0.24 and rail-head movement with twist 0.43 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 53 by flange width, 1 by sizing ratio; the next lighter, W27X84: flange 10.00 in narrower than the 10.50 in the details need. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

New cantilever column for a 12.5-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257). The tapered haunch on the W14X159 needs column continuity plates, which clash with the bracing gussets on a new column web: the lightest heavier W14 that needs none; The W14X211 chosen for the crane gives base drift ratio 2.13 > 0.9: the lightest heavier W14 within the drift and torsion ratios.

Set by the tie sizing: the column face moves out from 20 in (to at most 29 in, as far as the new column's twist and drift allow: the girder offset from the column axis is the lever of the eccentric reaction and of the longitudinal force at the seat) until the tie passes its imposed-movement and strength checks.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
